reviews.title: Not worth the money, definitely not for Japanese beginners.
reviews.text:
I paid $100 for a full year of Praktika because they advertise AI-powered language learning. After using it to study Japanese as a complete beginner, I’m very disappointed.
The app does not feel like real AI. The responses and lesson flow come across as rigid and mechanical rather than adaptive or intelligent. Even after setting the level to beginner so I could build fundamentals properly, the program moves far too quickly. Early on it asks me to answer questions in Japanese that require vocabulary and structures I haven’t been taught yet. That’s frustrating and counterproductive.
This does not feel like a program designed for people who are serious about learning a language from the ground up. The pacing and structure make it hard to actually absorb the material.
For comparison, I’ve learned more and progressed more comfortably with a free Japanese learning podcast on Spotify. At $100 for the year, Praktika simply isn’t delivering enough value. I would not recommend it if you’re looking for a solid, well-paced way to learn Japanese (or possibly any language) from scratch.

reviews.title: Frustrating, unreliable and not fit for learning Japanese
reviews.text:
This app is absolutely awful for learning Japanese. It constantly gives errors and doesn’t work in the way you would expect from a proper language-learning app.

The AI is particularly frustrating. Even when you give it very clear and specific instructions — for example, to only use hiragana and romaji, with no English translation — it simply does whatever it wants. It regularly ignores the instructions and produces something completely different from what you asked for, making it very difficult to use for structured Japanese practice.

You also can’t properly practise writing Japanese because you can’t draw/write characters — you can only speak. For a Japanese-learning app, this is a huge limitation.

On top of that, I couldn’t find a clear way to cancel the free trial, and I was charged for a full year of an app that I’m not going to use.

Overall, a very disappointing and frustrating experience. The app feels unfinished, the AI doesn’t reliably follow instructions, and I wouldn’t recommend it if your goal is to genuinely learn Japanese.

reviews.title: Surprisingly Bad
reviews.text:
The UI looks good, but the UX was horrible. The AI engineering needs serious work. I cannot believe how frustrating trying to use this app has been.

I’m already an intermediate level Japanese speaker and I got the app to up my game. Instead, I spent most of my time correcting mistakes it made on the simplest words and grammar. Additionally, it spoke all of the written text including the phonetic romaji that followed the katana or hiragana. This redundancy is not only annoying, it makes learning difficult and tedious. When I asked it to stop, it did, but only briefly. 

I switched to Italian and had different, but equally disappointing interface issues. 

The app couldn’t learn when corrected and the same mistakes were made repeated. 

To make matters worse, I can’t get my money back because I purchased the app from the App Store.

Final conclusion: Create your own agent that will actually be intelligent instead of wasting your money.

reviews.title: Definitely needs major improvements, but it is a decent idea. The advertisement was a bit misleading
reviews.text:
The app itself is pretty decent, but the speech recognition is frustrating. When I speak a full sentence, it usually understands me pretty well. But when I’m practicing a single short word, especially smaller/common words, it will sometimes just refuse to recognize what I’m saying no matter how many times I repeat it or how clearly I speak. Then I’m forced to type the answer just to get past the lesson, which defeats the whole purpose of using the speaking exercises.

The advertising also made it sound like the app would actively correct your pronunciation if you pronounced something incorrectly. In my experience, it mostly just tells you how to pronounce the word and then checks what you enter through the microphone. I haven’t really seen the detailed pronunciation correction that was advertised.

I was considering paying for the subscription, but the speech recognition issues are frustrating enough that I don’t think I will.

reviews.title: Needs improvement
reviews.text: I’ve tried all languages and was initially impressed with the possibility of learning by talking, but soon noticed the shortcoming of AI tutors. The voice recognition either accepts what you’ve said, or interpret it as something else, but it would not help you to correct your pronunciation. A human tutor would know how to speak to you with the words you’ve already learnt, introducing new phrases and grammar step by step, not talking to you in complex sentences that that the user doesn’t understand.  For non-Latin languages, it is essential to teach how to read, e.g. Cyrillic alphabet for Russian, hiragana and katagana for Japanese, and Hangul for Korean, pinyin and tones for Chinese, however, the apps skipped this step and immediately shows you those written languages without explanation.

reviews.title: Better conversation than duo, but worse than most other apps.

I didn’t mean to get the app in the first place. It said I could do “10 days free”, then I clicked to do that and it somehow purchased a year. I used it for a few weeks anyhow, to try to get my moneys worth.

I mostly do the custom scenarios, because the “lessons” are exceptionally bad. They also can’t really be done hands free, and I definitely want it to be hands free. The ‘Practice’ calls can be done hands free though. I would sometimes use it while driving.

Problems I noticed wth the practice calls:
1. I often had to give custom instructions at the beginning of the call, because it has a set pattern it always wants to use. I always had a bunch of custom instructions I kept in the notes app, so I could quickly copy/paste them over at the start of conversations.  

2. It would still frequently forget instructions. Like, if I was learning some new words, I might ask it to say the word at the start of the sentence. It would do that for like 4-5 sentences then stop.

3. By FAR the most annoying issue is that the LLM isn’t really trained on your voice. They have a model to transcribe your voice to words, then they have a separate model to send those words as text to the AI. The issue is, the voice transcriber was not good at figuring out which word you’re using if they sound the same. So like, if we’re talking about a third person, I might say “llamó” (he called), but it would it was “llamo” (I call). Then the AI would tell me I was wrong. 

Or when I asked the difference betw

reviews.title: Tutor mispronounces words
reviews.text:
This is absolutely frustrating! I’m learning German. The ai tutor is mispronouncing words and completely misunderstanding my words. Mispronunciation Example: when I got something right, the tutor would say “wunderbar” (wonderful) but pronounce the w like an English w. That would be completely incorrect in German. I’m a beginner and was able to catch that. 

Misunderstanding example: during a counting game, I was supposed to say the next number after the number the tutor said. We were working with 0-5. The Ai added a trick question - fünf (5) and I responded with sechs (6). The ai was expecting me to go back to null (0) but said that I said vier (4). “Vier” sounds nothing like “sechs”. When I said “wundershön” (beautiful) it thought I was mispronouncing “wandern”(hiking). Native German speakers understand how I pronounce “wundershön” just fine. To top it off, the tutor didn’t clarify if “wandern” was what I was trying to say. It just jumped into trying to practice sentences with that word. 

I also noted when I said nothing, it would indicate that I gave a full and completely correct answer.

reviews.text:
I’m learning Korean and neither of the male Korean avatars that are on their adverts are actually on the app! The app versions even on fully paid access, have much more basic animations, graphics and mouth movements. Min Jun sounds Indian when he’s speaking English! Then the voice changes to several different voices for different word or letter sounds.

It could be really good but the adverts are a lie and that really lets it down. It’s not what you think you’re paying for.

reviews.title: Pricey
reviews.text: Honestly I just downloaded but considering the fact that there is high chance I will stop using the app not really motivated to subscribe. Not to mention its too pricey. Not even sure why. I got a bumble lifetime subscription for 69£ while this ‘duo lingo’ wants 99£ PER year?! Is it greed? Is it ignorance or is there a reason behind it? I am not trying to be rude I genuinely wonder.

reviews.title: Why did you remove the best and the most liked Avatar with the best British accent?
reviews.text: There was this avatar with 297 likes and you removed it. You have to re add him again, I was able to learn the correct pronanciation from him. The other avatars are not clear or catchy like his accent. Are you going to re add? he had afro hair with 297 likes

reviews.title: What???
reviews.text:
Starting at the most basic level, knowing zero Spanish and it immediately starts speaking in long paragraphs at high speed. Not sure how I’m supposed to learn like that when it hasn’t even explained a single one of those words. I thought it was just me, but no, I tried several lessons and they were all the same. 

Also having to hold down the microphone button to speak is very  annoying. I’d rather it be like a conversation and just speak to it.

reviews.title: It’s not free
reviews.text: It said it was free and after filling up all the information is asking for me to pay even though in the middle of the button it say is that start free  when you click on it that doesn’t work that takes you automatically to payment for £99 so this is not correct. Very disappointing so do not trust this app.

reviews.title: No response from support
reviews.text: I've tried to contact the support team several times with no response. I have not used this app since the free trial yet I've been charged for a premium subscription despite contacting immediately for cancellation. Apple or no help and neither other developers. Very disappointing experience I hope the developer sort out their customer support.

reviews.title: Bad account management and rough for starters. Otherwise decent practice.
reviews.text:
Update has killed the AI‘s ability to understand most things said… after a full month I am requesting a partial refund.

The accounts being tied to Apple or Google and not openly accessible is silly. Because I used private relay it isn’t possible to log into my non Apple devices. It is obviously a feature that people want because I found multiple places online talking about it. It is even part of their faq. I would like to use it with any of the devices I have.

Additionally, the app tends to start you at a more intermediate level than a true beginner. After a month with the other apps, I am starting to get somewhere with Praktika. I will use it for the duration of my subscription but then will let it lapse.
